about: The course is hands-on and built around labs. You run your code in the simulator from the first week, and on the 1/10-scale car once you have one.
It is written for senior undergraduates and graduate students who want to work on perception, planning, control and applied machine learning.

faq.q: How long is the course and how much time does it take?
faq.a: Pick 4, 10 or 15 weeks; the full course fills a semester. The syllabus plans two 80-minute classes a week, with labs done outside class.
faq.note: TODO(content): add student hours per week once Cedric or Rahul gives them (see plans[].effort_note).

faq.q: When does it start, and can I join late?
faq.a: The material is open on the course site all year, so start whenever you like and go at your own pace. University offerings follow their own term dates.

faq.q: Do I need to buy and build the car?
faq.a: Not to start. Tutorial 2 sets up the simulator, and your code runs there first. The course's three races run on the 1/10-scale car; the build docs show how to build one.

faq.q: How do I sign up and get help?
faq.a: There is nothing to sign up for: the lectures, slides and labs are open on the course site. Ask questions in the RoboRacer Slack. If your university runs the course, its staff come first.
On your own, you are not. Universities that run the course grade their students with their own weights; the course site publishes rubrics for the labs, races and final project.

faq.q: How do I get access as an instructor?
faq.a: Email contact@roboracer.ai with your university, your names and what you would like to teach. We set you up with an instructor account on the course platform.

faq.q: Do I have to teach the whole course?
faq.a: No. Start from the 4-, 10- or 15-week plan and add or drop modules to fit your students' background, your term and their interests.

faq.q: Can I use my own logo and colors?
faq.a: Yes. Your copy of the course carries your university or lab logo and colors.

faq.q: Can I add or replace material?
faq.a: Yes. In Studio you delete the units you don't need, add new ones with text, slides, videos and quizzes, and publish when ready.
That depends on your class size and how many cars you run. Slides, recorded lectures, lab starter code and grading rubrics are ready, so there is less to prepare.

faq.q: How are students graded, and can I prevent cheating?
faq.a: You set the weights for quizzes, labs and races, and the passing grade. Honor-code agreements, randomized question pools and limited attempts help check real understanding.
Students sign in on the Courses portal and enroll in your course. Send them your course link.

faq.q: Can I reuse the course next semester?
faq.a: Yes. Re-run it in Studio, rename it, update the dates and the team, and it is ready for a new class.
Email contact@roboracer.ai or ask in the RoboRacer Slack. The Open edX course staff guide covers every Studio task.
